questions.question: Why do people work?
options: Because they enjoy their job every day
Only because they are bored at home and want to kill time
To earn money and help others
People don't work
questions.explanation: People work to earn money for living and to help others.

questions.question: Chrumko notices that mom is getting ready for work in the morning, even though it's raining. Why does she go?
options: She gets money for work, which the family uses to pay for everything
She's bored at home and had an argument with Chrumko, so she wants to leave
She likes walking in the rain because it calms her down
She has no other choice, even though she is never paid for work
questions.explanation: Mom gets money for work, which the family uses to pay for everything they need.

questions.question: What is the importance of people's work in society?
options: None
All jobs are useless, people can do everything without help
Work is only about money
Teachers, doctors and others improve life for everyone through their work
questions.explanation: Work creates value, earns money and makes the world a better place.

questions.question: With the money from work, a family pays for rent, food and school costs.
questions.explanation: Mom gets a salary and the family uses it to pay for everything they need.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: People work to get money.
Work can also help other people.
Work is useless and nobody spends time on it.
questions.explanation: Work earns money and at the same time helps others.

questions.question: Match each item with its meaning.
matchRight: Rent, food and school costs are paid from it
questions.explanation: Work brings money and also helps others.

questions.question: Sort the examples by the reason why people work.
dragLabels: Paying for electricity and water from a salary
questions.explanation: Two reasons why people work: earning money and helping others.

questions.question: Put in order what Chrumko gradually realizes about work.
orderItems: In the morning Chrumko sees mom getting ready for work, even though it's raining
He asks why she has to go every day
Mom explains that she gets money for work to pay for rent, food and school costs
questions.explanation: Chrumko gradually understands the relationship between work and everyday life.

questions.question: Do all adults do the same work?
options: Yes, everyone does the same so that nobody is left out
No, everyone does something different and together they keep the world running
Adults don't work
All adults are builders or doctors, no other occupation exists
questions.explanation: Everyone does something different, but together these jobs keep the world running.

questions.question: Chrumko is going to school. How many different jobs does he see?
options: Only one, a builder
None, because all adults work from home
He sees only three jobs that exist: doctor, teacher and builder
A bus driver, a teacher, sidewalk repairmen, a shop assistant and a postman
questions.explanation: Chrumko sees a driver, a teacher, repairmen, a shop assistant, a postman and others.

questions.question: A bus driver, a teacher and a postman do the same work.
questions.explanation: Each of them does a different job, but together they keep the world running.

questions.question: Match each worker with what they do.
questions.explanation: Each occupation has its own role.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Different occupations complement each other.
All adults do exactly the same thing.
Some people work with people, others with things or information.
questions.explanation: Not everyone does the same – there are many different jobs.

questions.question: Sort the activities by type of work.
questions.explanation: Jobs can be divided into working with people, creating physical things and working with information.

questions.question: Why is it important to have different occupations?
options: One occupation would be enough, but people don't want to be the same
Everything is random
Different skills together ensure that society functions
It's not important
questions.explanation: Every job counts – different occupations together help the world function.

questions.question: Does everyone get the same money for their work?
options: No, the amount of salary depends on many criteria
Yes, always, so that nobody is treated unfairly
Nobody ever gets anything, because adults work for free
Everyone gets the same
questions.explanation: The amount of salary is influenced by education, skills, responsibility and the time devoted to work.

questions.question: Salary is paid once a month into a bank account.
questions.explanation: Chrumko's dad receives his salary once a month into his account.

questions.question: Chrumko is talking with dad about salaries. What does dad explain to him?
options: Money arrives in the bank account every day, so they can use it that day
He gets a salary once a month and the family pays for everything needed during the month from it
Money is always spent right away
The salary never arrives, because adults get food for work, not money
questions.explanation: Money from work needs to be divided wisely so that it lasts.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: The amount of salary depends on education and skills.
Greater responsibility often brings a higher salary.
Everyone gets the same salary regardless of occupation.
questions.explanation: Salaries differ – not everyone gets the same amount.

questions.question: Match each factor with its meaning.
matchRight: More expertise often means a higher salary
Hours, days or months of work count
Greater responsibility brings a higher salary
Arrives once a month into the account
questions.explanation: Several factors influence the amount of salary.

questions.question: Sort things by whether they affect the amount of salary.
questions.explanation: Salary is influenced by education, skills, responsibility and time.

questions.question: Why does a salary need to be divided wisely?
options: It's not important, because everything is free
Everything can be bought right away, because money is endless
It has to last for everything needed during the whole month
It makes no sense
questions.explanation: A salary is a reward for work and needs to be planned so that it covers the whole month.

questions.question: Why is time important in work?
options: Many jobs are paid by the hour – more hours, more earned
Time is useless, at the end of the month you always get the same amount of money anyway
Time is never counted
You are paid only per day, not per hour
questions.explanation: In many jobs, the more hours a person works, the more they earn.

questions.question: Chrumko sees his older brother helping the neighbor. What is he doing?
options: Playing in the garden, and thereby scaring off thieves
Sitting at the neighbor's house playing cards with him
Doing nothing
Helping all morning in the garden – gathering leaves, raking grass and carrying branches
questions.explanation: Brother devotes time and effort to the work and receives a small reward.

questions.question: The time we devote to work doesn't matter for the reward.
questions.explanation: Time and effort count in work.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: In work only time counts, nobody cares about effort.
The time we devote to work affects the reward.
Effort and quality of work matter too.
questions.explanation: Time, effort and quality of work all count.

questions.question: Match each situation with what it means.
matchRight: Covers all hours worked in a month
questions.explanation: Reward is related to both time and effort.

questions.question: Sort the statements by method of payment.
dragLabels: Covers a whole month of work
Salary for all hours worked in the month
questions.explanation: With hourly pay the number of hours matters, a monthly salary covers all hours in the month.

questions.question: Put in order what Chrumko realizes about time and work.
orderItems: Chrumko sees that his brother is helping the neighbor in the garden
Brother works all morning – gathering leaves, raking grass and carrying branches
After the work he receives a small reward
Chrumko understands that time and effort count in work
questions.explanation: Chrumko gradually understands the value of time in work.

questions.question: What is productivity?
options: Working as slowly as possible, because every job is paid by the hour
Working with focus so that we get more done in less time
Doing nothing
Interrupting work all the time and taking breaks to play on the phone
questions.explanation: When we work attentively and with focus, we get more done in less time.

questions.question: Chrumko is doing his homework and keeps looking at his phone. What happens?
options: The homework takes him little time, the phone magically does the homework for him
He can't do the homework, so he'd rather start playing
Everything goes fast, he has two eyes after all
The homework takes him a very long time, because he gets distracted
questions.explanation: Distraction and frequent interruptions make work longer.

questions.question: Removing distractions helps you work more productively.
questions.explanation: Without interruptions, work goes faster and without stress.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Preparing everything needed before starting helps.
Interruptions improve the quality of work.
Focusing on one task at a time increases productivity.
questions.explanation: Interruptions reduce productivity, they don't increase it.

questions.question: Match each activity with its effect.
matchLeft: Working on one task at a time
matchRight: Better focus on a specific task
questions.explanation: Different habits affect productivity in different ways.

questions.question: Sort the activities by their effect on productivity.
questions.explanation: Focus, preparation and removing distractions increase productivity.

questions.question: How can Chrumko increase his productivity when doing homework?
options: Spend more time on the homework without any change or progress in his work
Play while studying
Put the phone away, prepare everything needed and work with focus
Look at the phone after every sentence
questions.explanation: Focused work without interruptions is the key to higher productivity.
